problem: A value-producing validator must not be used only for exception side effects, and a container replacement must not hide mutation of borrowed primitive builtin inputs. Catalog error metadata alone does not block the native CLI when emitted diagnostics remain warnings.
change: Promote default and actual diagnostic severity to ERROR for both qualified rules. Recognition logic and ownership boundaries are byte-identical to the published warning release after normalizing those two severity sites per rule. No autofix is offered.

warningRelease.distributions: Exact PyPI versions verified with wheels and source distributions.

candidateWheel.source_equivalence: Only default and emitted severities changed from the verified warning release; all other rule source bytes are identical.

validation.cliContract: Violations exit1 and emit error diagnostics. Consumed checked values, copies before writes and explicit None commands exit0.
validation.qualificationReuse: The 3,000-file immutable warning corpus and its 3 inspected true policy matches, 0 known false positives and measured bounded performance remain applicable because recognition source is unchanged. No new corpus precision or performance claim is made.

fullVerification.note: Local private-reference scanning delegates to trusted exact-head CI, which remains required before merge.

scope: Source-proven validation and borrowed primitive builtin-container transformations. Preserve native command/result protocols, framework/exception assertions and unsupported dynamic contracts. This is bounded enforcement, not a proof of arbitrary program purity.

campaign.countingPolicy: Distinct evidenced defects, maintained-owner reviews, native protocol boundaries, qualification/remediation and packaged enforcement reviews. Repeated tests, generated vectors and cosmetic variants are not passes.
